walkthroughs.body_html: From inside out: core (fusion), radiative zone, convective zone, photosphere, chromosphere and corona. The core reaches ~15 million K.
Sunspots appear darker because they are ~1500 K cooler. They follow an ~11-year cycle. Twisted magnetic fields can snap, producing flares and coronal mass ejections.
The solar wind streams charged particles outward. Earth's magnetic field channels them to the poles, where they collide with the atmosphere and create the aurora borealis and aurora australis.

Hotter than surroundings
Hollow

mcqs.q: Why is Jupiter classified as a gas giant?
options: Its bulk is mostly hydrogen and helium with no defined solid surface.
It is made of fire.
It is mostly air like Earth's atmosphere.
Because clouds block them.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a solar eclipse and a lunar eclipse?
options: Because clouds block them.
Solar eclipses happen by day, lunar at night - that is the only difference.
In a solar eclipse the Moon blocks the Sun; in a lunar eclipse Earth's shadow covers the Moon.
Lunar eclipses are more dangerous.

mcqs.q: Why don't we have a solar eclipse every new moon?
options: The Moon's orbit is tilted, so it usually passes above or below the Sun's apparent position.
Because clouds block them.
It is made of fire.
Eclipses happen randomly.
